description: CyberChef differential cases. Every case cites a `reference_source` a reviewer can check: either a value observed by running upstream CyberChef via tools/cyberchef-reference/capture.mjs, or a published specification both implementations follow. Cases are data, never generated from rx-chef.

encodings.reference_source: Where the expected value comes from. Required. Use a specification reference (e.g. 'RFC 4648 section 10') or 'observed: CyberChef <version>' for a value read off upstream.

verdicts.exact: rx-chef output must equal the reference byte for byte after normalization.
verdicts.documented_difference: rx-chef deliberately differs; `divergence` explains why and `reference` records what CyberChef produces.
verdicts.not_comparable: The operation is excluded from differential comparison; `divergence` gives the reason.
verdicts.unverified: No reference value has been recorded yet.

cases.reference_source: RFC 3986: space is percent-encoded, sub-delims and '!' are not

cases.divergence: A truncated varint (final byte with the continuation bit set) is incomplete. Both implementations return the bits accumulated so far rather than reporting an error; recorded here so the behaviour is not changed by accident.
Non-deterministic: the operation produces fresh random bytes on every run.
Performs network I/O, so the result depends on an external service.
